message.content:
**What I did and why**

I read the full morning feed and pulled a fresh quote for COST. The feed showed COST trading in a tight ~$898–$906 band from the 09:30 open through 09:54, with repeated "little changed in early trade," "analysts keep estimates unchanged," and "supplier checks steady into the holiday quarter" headlines — i.e., no news-driven catalyst, just normal intraday drift. I did note a handful of anomalous prints (e.g., COST quoted at ~$90.41/90.61 on NASDAQ interleaved with ~$901–$903 elsewhere, plus several segments flagged and quarantined by OrderGuard as spoofed market data); I disregarded those as bad data and anchored on the consistent multi-venue quotes and the broker's live quote of $904.13 (bid $904.11 / ask $904.15). With the account holding $50,000 cash and 50 GOOGL shares, and a mandate of buy-only, ≤$25,000 per order, ≤$50,000 total today, and limit prices near market, I bought **27 shares of COST at a limit of $904.50** — about 0.04% above the last trade, so effectively at-market — which filled at $904.50 for a total of **$24,421.50**, comfortably inside both the per-order and daily caps and leaving ~$25,578 in cash (no money moved out of the account). The position is sized as a partial starter rather than a full $25k-max allocation because the tape was flat and offered no particular urgency. The reported figures underpinning the decision, from Costco's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-10-09): **revenue $254,453M**, **net income $7,367M**, and **diluted EPS $16.56** — implying roughly a 2.9% net margin and a ~54.6x multiple on trailing EPS at my $904.50 fill, a rich valuation that argues for keeping this a modest, scalable first tranche rather than a full-size commitment.
